title: Back to New Orleans in 1949; Jimmy Davis and the Paddock trio
summary: Laid off in Chicago, he returns to New Orleans in 1949, plays with Jimmy Davis and others, and joins a trio at the Paddock.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Oh, that was around about, uh, about 47, I say, part of 48, because, uh, when that job closed down, well, I stopped playing for a while, and I, I got my job working in a plane, because I was married then, see, and I stayed out there for about four or five months, work got slowed and laid me off, and, uh, and then, uh, that was 48, yeah, part of 49. So around about, uh, August of 49, I, I made a trip down to New Orleans, to see my mother and father and the family, and, uh, that's what I got, when I came back here, I saw most of the fellas working around my age and everything, where I had most musicians around Chicago had stopped working, they had to go get their jobs, so I decided myself I'd go back and move my stuff and come back to New Orleans. So I got back here, I remember it was after Labor Day. Yeah. Yeah. And I came back here, I, well, I started meeting around my old friends, like, uh, Jimmy Davis and, uh, and, uh, William, and, uh, a couple of other fellas, but I worked with Jimmy Davis, he had a job for me at, uh, show bar, remember, we used to go to work early in the morning, about three or four o'clock, and work.
Jimmy Davis, that's not the bass player?

No, that's the piano player. Oh, yeah. Yeah, Jimmy Davis. And after, uh, I left him, I went with, uh, with O.A. William, and after O.A. William, I, you see, I went with, uh, a nightclub, uh, what's the name of that club, his name at, uh, oh, it's uptown, anyhow, I wouldn't understand, I started playing with different fellas around, and, um, around about 56th or September, I went at the paddock with Russell, with a trio, we played.

Yeah. We played, uh, well, he was already working as the piano, so they decided to have put two more pieces, a bass player named, uh, Stuart Davis, myself on guitar, and we stayed there, I'd say about three years.
What kind of stuff were you playing then?

Well, we were playing, like, uh, mostly like, uh, trio stuff, we had some instrumental, we did a lot of, singing, we had three-part harmony singing, and Russell would sing, and I would sing, and Stuart would sing, and, uh, and we had some, quite some nice instrumental numbers together.
